summary: FidelityManager still has an uncovered PolicyConfig no-execute/plain-data boundary after PR #274: constructor copy and pure-policy config validation can dereference or compare malformed metatable-backed config data before primitive/plain-data rejection.
evidence: PR #274 head 60de91b49338249c1ded74db0d722921ce2fb55d hardens PolicyInputs, registration ordering, transition-hook failure atomicity, and same-entity callback reentrancy, but does not add a PolicyConfig plain-data boundary.
At that head FidelityManager.new(config) calls copyConfig(sourceConfig) before validateConfig; copyConfig reads every config field, so a top-level __index metatable can execute before rejection.

validateConfig performs comparisons/arithmetic/finiteness checks on config scalars without first proving primitive number type; malformed metatable-backed scalar values can therefore reach comparison metamethods.
evaluatePolicy(inputs, config, currentLevel) accepts an optional PolicyConfig and calls validateConfig on it; there is no top-level type/metatable guard before config field reads.

Current main tests/fidelity_manager.luau covers infinite/overflow numeric config values, while PR #274 tests/fidelity_manager_rejected_step_atomicity.luau covers hostile PolicyInputs and callback atomicity; neither covers hostile PolicyConfig metatables or wrong-typed scalar no-execute behavior.
Open PR search found no separate Fidelity PolicyConfig hardening PR, so this is not duplicated by the active Fidelity source/audit work inspected in #274/#292.

metadata.recommendedAfter: Integrate PR #274 first because the source scope overlaps src/shared/Physics/FidelityManager.luau.
recommendedAcceptance: reject non-table or metatable-backed PolicyConfig before first field dereference in new() and evaluatePolicy()
primitive-type-check every numeric config scalar before equality/comparison/arithmetic/finiteness operations
prove hostile __index/__lt/__le callbacks execute zero times
preserve default policy outputs, deterministic behavior, O(1) evaluation, and existing #274 transaction invariants
source-only validation; no Roblox Studio evidence
